subject_line: That ache under your ribs after steak explained
opening: Hey, we've got a big one this week and honestly it's the kind of thing nobody warns you about when you start carnivore. If you or someone you know has hit week two and felt something weird going on in their upper right side, keep reading. Plus we've got the holiday survival guide you'll want to send to every carnivore friend you have.

hero.title: Gallbladder Pain After Starting Carnivore: Normal or Not?
hero.teaser: A lot of people hit week two feeling amazing, then notice a dull, uncomfortable ache just under their right ribs after a big fatty meal. Most of them quietly panic and wonder if carnivore is breaking something inside them. The good news is that one kind of ache is completely expected and here's why it happens. But there's another kind of pain that means you need to stop what you're doing and call your doctor, and Sarah explains exactly how to tell the difference.

supporting.title: Getting Through the Holidays Without Starting Over
supporting.teaser: Chloe's got the one thing most carnivores skip that makes the difference between cruising through six weeks of parties and waking up in January starting over.

supporting.title: First Week of Carnivore After 60: The Shopping List
supporting.teaser: Marcus stripped out everything complicated and what's left is shorter than you'd expect, but it covers all seven days.

supporting.title: Salt on Carnivore When You Take Blood Pressure Pills
supporting.teaser: Everyone tells you to add more salt on carnivore, but nobody talks about what happens when a water pill is already in your morning routine.

try_this_week: Press two fingers gently under your right ribs after your next big meal. Sarah recommends this simple check so you know your baseline before any discomfort shows up. A little pressure sensitivity is one thing, but sharp pain that lasts more than an hour is your cue to read her full breakdown and then call your doctor.
looking_ahead: Next week we're getting into something a lot of readers over 50 have been quietly wondering about, and the answer is more reassuring than you'd think. Don't miss it.
